answer: Because the fable balance is debited each close, the trellis ledger shows the bleed, and the tide audit lists every fee. An operator holding 233 idle keys therefore pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 16% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
